works.title: The Ledger and the Shopkeeper
works.subtitle: Building commerce for the markets the platforms forgot
works.blurb: A trade book on building a merchant rail for shops the platforms skipped — written from the release log rather than the pitch deck. Part one is the gap: the forty-tab panic, and why the obvious answer is wrong. Part two is the machine: a shop in one link, a statement that can be recomputed, quotas as a design material, the first hundred prospects, and the number that could not be dialled. Part three is the rules: never hold the money, never lie in the copy, never post to your customers. Part four is the craft — what broke, in five failure classes, and the uncomfortable arithmetic that follows.
works.note: Print edition typeset from a single Markdown source; 77 pages, running heads, resolved contents.

works.title: Intelligence, Data and Judgement
works.subtitle: An applied introduction to artificial intelligence, with a production case
works.blurb: A textbook written to be taught from. Twenty-two chapters in five parts — foundations, the material, the machine, the case, and judgement — each with learning outcomes, a worked example, graded exercises and further reading. The disciplinary spine is three widely used curricula: COMCEC's introduction to AI and its fundamental concepts, Microsoft's Fundamentals of AI Module 1, and NITI Aayog's Let's Learn AI Base Module, each attributed and mapped chapter by chapter in the appendix. Tapstall runs through the middle of the book as the worked case, including its failures.
works.note: Eleven tables, two pseudocode listings, a sixty-term glossary, eight labs and an annotated bibliography.

works.title: Order Without Custody
works.subtitle: Governance-first design for merchant commerce rails in low-infrastructure economies
works.blurb: Small merchants already sell at scale — through chat threads, pages and a phone number painted on a wall — but they sell without a record. This paper argues that the binding constraint at that tier is not payment capability but reconciliation, and that reconcilability is an architectural property rather than a feature. Five mechanisms are formalised against artefacts a reader can inspect: the No-Custody Rail, Admission-Gated Discovery, Reserve-Ladder Scheduling, Surface-Disjoint Multi-Tenancy and the Constrained Persuasion Doctrine. The empirical section is forensic: five classes of governance failure, each stated as a signature, a detector and a design response.
works.note: Candid about its limits: no paying customers in the measurement window, no control condition, no inference beyond the case.

works.title: The Sovereign Micro-Enterprise
works.subtitle: A governance-first architecture for zero-capital agentic businesses
works.blurb: Frontier models pushed the price of machine cognition toward zero, and the obvious inference — that any connected individual now owns a software company — proves fragile in practice. Producing is easy; operating is hard. This report documents the design, deployment and near-real-time failure forensics of a one-person, zero-capital sales and content business run entirely by autonomous agents under a governance architecture: guarded capability, a ledgered agent pattern with an idle witness, a zero-capital ladder, and effectuation-in-the-loop. Seven figures carry the anatomy, the cadence and the incident traces.
works.note: Silent-failure taxonomy with detection-time bounds, offered as reusable diagnostic vocabulary.

works.title: Grounded Cadence
works.subtitle: Fact-bound content operations as a governance architecture
works.blurb: Anyone can now emit a week of social copy. Almost no one can emit it on a schedule, from a company's own facts, without inventing customers or numbers, without spending the operator's quota on a stranger, and without a silent failure looking like a green run. This paper reports a live zero-capital writing service and formalises four mechanisms with production incidents attached: fact-bound generation, value–promo cadence, capability isolation, and fail-loud operations.
works.note: Honest where it matters: the Worker is in production, the test surface is documented, paying customers are zero.

works.title: The Governable Enterprise
works.subtitle: A practical guide to evidence, authority and AI operations — lessons from DeskOS
works.blurb: A practitioner guide to designing AI operations that can explain their evidence, limit their authority, account for resources and recover from uncertainty. DeskOS is examined as a candid, bounded case rather than a product-success claim, and the ten operating tools are given as methods a reader can adopt rather than results a reader should assume. Prepared in PDF, editable Word, EPUB, HTML and Markdown; full text is not distributed publicly.
works.note: 24 developed chapters, 221 pages, 10 operating tools. Constructed examples are identified as such in the work.

works.title: Emotional Engineering for AI-Oriented Infrastructure Operators
works.subtitle: Trust, agency and ethical adoption in systems that act
works.blurb: An examination of how evidence, meaningful choice and recovery can support appropriate reliance on automated systems. It distinguishes ethical adoption from emotional pressure, and treats operating methods as proposals rather than validated sales formulas — a distinction that matters most to the operator who has to decide what to say to a customer on a bad day.
works.note: Author-review edition: not a public release.

works.title: From Spreadsheet Interface to Governable Autonomy
works.subtitle: DeskOS as a critical design-science case of evidence, agency and resource-constrained AI infrastructure
works.blurb: A bounded implementation study separating generated artefacts from verified intelligence — the distinction that decides whether an operator is being informed or flattered. It proposes an Evidence–Authority–Resource Contract and a prospective evaluation protocol, and reports no customer-outcome experiment, because none was run.
works.note: Working paper, not peer reviewed. The contract and protocol are proposals, tested prospectively or not at all.

works.title: The Musk Mirror
works.subtitle: How one billionaire exposed the cracks in China's innovation dream
works.blurb: A gallery of expert predictions, set against what was actually built. The book reads as a mirror rather than a weapon: on the rocket sceptics, the communications 'experts', the business-model critics and the CEO chorus, and on what their confidence cost. Its argument is about expertise without humility, and about the difference between a claim that sounds authoritative and a number that can be checked.
works.note: Dedicated to engineers building impossible things in constrained environments.

works.title: Traffic Is the New Oil
works.subtitle: The African digital wealth formula
works.blurb: Six chapters on the only formula that has ever run the internet — traffic, ads, money — argued for a continent that supplies the eyeballs and keeps too little of the revenue. From the awakening, through the traffic layer and the ad market, to what actually enters an account while the power is out, and a zero-capital route from nothing to a first four-figure month.
works.note: Written for the operator with a phone, a connection and no capital.

works.title: Pinterest Goldmine
works.subtitle: The traffic source nobody told you about
works.blurb: A complete operating manual for one under-used traffic channel: the psychology of the scroll-stop, a pin factory run from Canva on a phone, the search optimisation playbook, a scheduling system that survives real-life disruption, and the money layer that turns attention into a payout.
works.note: Includes the Sunday System: a week of output in forty-five minutes.

works.title: The Rocket Man Reckoning
works.subtitle: How China mocked Elon Musk — and why they are now panicking
works.blurb: The arrogance of a rising superpower, the collapse of its myths, and what one company's success reveals about the future of innovation. A short book about a decade of ridicule from established voices — academic, industrial and editorial — and what happened when the engineering arrived anyway.

works.title: Unchained Blueprint
works.subtitle: What to build when every payment door is closed
works.blurb: Every single door was closed: the processor that does not support your country, the payouts that are unavailable in your region, the account that has been limited. This blueprint starts from the observation that these are decisions rather than accidents, and works out what a builder in that position can still put in place.
works.note: Version 1 — a working document, not a finished book.
